EXIT=1). The two actioned items in the coordinator's message (remove the copies, fix the tests: line) are both done. What the delta does not do is collapse promote.py's own _git invocation, which is still a second git runner in the package and is what the fragment's 'one git invocation' sentence overstates.

findings.text: The fragment says 'the package holds one github-slug parser and one git invocation instead of three'. The tree at this head holds two git-invocation helpers in the package: imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:401 (_run_git, exported as run_git) and imas_codex/standard_names/promote.py:176 (_git), and release_notes.py:133 imports promote._git for its diff/show reads, so a reader is told a consolidation landed that did not. The 'three' is also unsupported for slug parsers: at 611ba81d3 the package held two (catalog_release._github_slug and release_notes._github_slug); promote.parse_pull_request_url parses a PR URL, not a remote slug. The landed repair is correct and the copy is genuinely gone; only the evidence prose overstates its reach. File the count as two helpers is unchanged and delete the 'one ... instead of three' claim, or fold the promote._git consumer onto run_git in the continuation node that closes release_notes' remaining exemptions.

The docstring still says 'release_notes imports _github_slug and _run_git from catalog_release at module level'. After this delta release_notes.py:29 imports the public spellings github_slug and run_git, so the comment names two private names that no longer cross that boundary and would mislead the next reader of the guard it documents. The test body is unaffected; only the prose is stale, and the delta is what made it stale.

The baseline_suite and after_suite command fields carry angle-bracket placeholders ('PYTHONPATH=<base tree> ... <the 14 files of the first round's gate>' and '<the 17 files named on the tests line>'), which the record contract forbids in a command field. The literal commands are recoverable from each log's own 'rev:'/'cmd:' header and from the manifest's now-exact tests: line, so nothing is lost; the two JSON blocks simply cannot be re-run as written. Substitute each log's header command.
